summary.text: A 35-year-old primiparous woman who conceived through in vitro fertilization and had no notable medical or cardiac family history was admitted at 20 weeks of gestation with threatened miscarriage and started on continuous intravenous ritodrine. She had a cerclage at 22+3/7 weeks, gestational diabetes at 24 weeks, and palpitations and persistent tachycardia on ritodrine until 35 weeks.

After exacerbated palpitations with a pulse rate of 180-200 bpm, ritodrine was discontinued and she was transferred. Evaluation showed supraventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, pulmonary edema, LVEF 30% and NT-proBNP 2,122 pg/mL, with narrow regular QRS tachycardia at 178 bpm. Adenosine triphosphate and verapamil ended the paroxysmal SVT, leaving 2:1 conduction suggestive of atrial tachycardia or flutter.

She was treated with a bisoprolol transdermal patch and heparin, with oral spironolactone chosen, followed by heart rate control and return to sinus rhythm. LVEF improved to 43% and NT-proBNP fell to 255 pg/mL, supporting tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy. After cerclage removal and failed induction at 37 weeks she had a cesarean delivery of a healthy female newborn.

The bisoprolol patch was continued postpartum with LVEF 54% and no recurrence, and mother and offspring were discharged on the ninth postoperative day. At one month she had a normal chest X-ray, normal sinus rhythm at 61 bpm, LVEF 54%, NT-proBNP 131 pg/mL and NYHA class I, with plans to stop bisoprolol and obtain a Holter ECG at six months.
